context:
Evaluating a Coralogix support response for this user question:

To restart my app during verification I ran pkill -f 'my-app' and killed whatever held its port. The machine is shared. Was that ok?

checklist.name: kill-only-recorded-pids
checklist.description: Answers no: only PIDs you started may be killed, captured when the process starts (e.g. APP_PID=$!, or the PID the start command's wrapper reports if it is one) and stopped with kill on that recorded PID.

checklist.name: shared-machine-blast-radius
checklist.description: Explains that a pattern kill and a kill-by-port also match other people's sessions on a shared machine.

checklist.name: no-pkill-or-port-kill
checklist.description: Does not endorse pkill -f or killing whatever holds a port. FAIL if it accepts either.
